checkpoints: Edits enqueue into the active document’s 120 ms trailing buffer instead of writing immediately.
A burst of edits saves once, with only the latest text, after 120 ms without another edit.
Retiring an active document preserves already-entered text that has not yet reached its timer deadline.
A synchronous navigation caused by persistence cannot be overwritten when an older select or close resumes.
Committed navigation visits retain their visit identifiers and copied breadcrumb entries.
Search preview remains a 40 ms cancellable trailing consumer.
The public workspace methods remain available.
forbidden_effects: Do not write every edit directly to the store.
Do not persist superseded intermediate values from the same coalesced burst.
Do not lose pending text when selection, close, or disposal retires the active document.
Do not allow an older select or close operation to overwrite navigation performed synchronously during persistence.
Do not collapse separate committed visits solely because their document identifiers match.
Do not change search-preview behavior or timing.
Do not change tests, configuration, dependencies, or public API shapes.
lifecycle_identity: Autosave buffering is per document, matching the existing BufferBank keyed by document id.
Each navigation visit carries both a document id and a visit identifier.
A scheduled trailing save remains associated with its latest queued value until it is flushed, cancelled, or superseded.
Committed breadcrumb entries are copies of visits rather than shared mutable visit objects.

obligations.text: An edit of the active document must push its text into that document’s existing trailing buffer rather than call store.write immediately.
The document buffer must wait 120 ms after the latest edit and then persist only that latest text.

Retiring an active view through selection, close, or disposal must preserve pending edited text, because navigation and persistence behavior must remain unchanged from the prior immediate-write behavior.

Operations that persist pending text must account for store subscribers running synchronously; if such a subscriber starts a newer navigation operation, the interrupted older operation must not subsequently replace that newer editor or projection state.
Only a retained selection may be committed to the navigation projection, and distinct retained visits must remain distinct even when they use the same document id.
The workspace must continue to expose select(id), edit(text), close(), selection(), and dispose().
Search preview must retain its existing 40 ms trailing scheduling and cancellation behavior.

ordering_barriers: Each newer edit must replace the previously scheduled value before the document’s trailing save consumes it.
Pending text must be persisted while retiring the corresponding active view so navigation, close, and disposal do not discard it.
After a callback-capable store write, an interrupted select or close must confirm it is still the current operation before publishing editor or projection state.
Projection commit must occur only for the selection operation whose editor visit was retained.
A cancelled or superseded timer must not later persist its former value.
preservation: Preserve workspace coordination of document visits.
Preserve persistence across selection, close, and disposal.
Preserve separation of document body, per-document buffer, and navigation projection responsibilities.
Preserve visit identifiers in document and projection sinks.
Preserve copied breadcrumb history for committed visits.
scope: Change editor autosave behavior in workspace business code.
Reuse the existing trailing utility and per-document BufferBank.
Handle retirement and synchronous navigation interactions needed to preserve existing navigation and persistence behavior.
Preserve tests, configuration, dependencies, and public documents.

push(text) { if (ticket !== null) timers.cancel(ticket); value = text; ticket = timers.schedule(flush, wait); }
const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };
